label: early original-phase steps (t=2..4) after a q has appeared
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase at absolute positions t=2..4 (peak at t=3), but only if the letter q was input at some earlier step. 99% of activation mass is in the original phase; it is silent at t=0,1, nearly silent at t>=6, and essentially never fires in the copy phase (a small tail fires at <DEL> for short sequences). Magnitude is highest when q occurred early and repeatedly: the top activations (~7.5) are all sequences beginning q q q, peaking at t=3 right after the q run. prev2_tok==q (lift 15.7x) and first_tok==q (9.8x) are the strongest single correlates. A q immediately before the current step (prev_tok==q with no earlier q) tends to give weak or no activation; the feature turns on about two steps after the q. The current input token identity matters little. Missed activations are mostly weak firings at t=5, and false positives are mostly t=4 steps right after a single late q.

issues: Main finding: the feature depends on how recently q appeared, not on whether q appeared at all. seen(q) lets in long-ago q's and misses this. At t=4 with exactly one q in the prefix (dev precision): q at position 0 gives 0.27, q at position 1 gives 0.85, q at position 2 gives 0.82, q at position 3 (the step just before) gives 0.16. A q four steps back, or a single q one step back at t=4, mostly does not fire. Together these are the false-positive class, and t=4 & seen(q) as a whole has precision only 0.55.

The claim 'a lone q immediately before the current step gives weak or no activation' is wrong at t=2 and t=3. t=2 with q only at position 1 has precision 0.84. t=3 with a single q at position 2 has precision 0.76. t=3 with a single q at position 0 has 0.93, and with a single q at position 1 has 0.99. The step right after a q fails only at t=4.
'Turns on about two steps after the q' is imprecise. The feature fires 1 to 3 steps after a q, inside the window t=2..4. One step after only counts when t<=3.

Claims that check out: zero activity at t=0..1; 99.4% of mass in the original phase; 0.6% at <DEL>; one copy-phase activation; t=3 peak (49% of mass); the top activations are all q q q at t=3; the lifts for prev2_tok==q (15.7x) and first_tok==q (9.8x); and the reported test scores (P 0.767, R 0.888, F1 0.823, mass recall 0.969, all reproduced).

Remaining misses with the refined predicate are mostly weak (about 0.01 to 0.04 of max), for example steps after a q at t=4 or t=5 and scattered steps with no q. Together they hold about 4.7% of the activation mass, which is acceptable noise.
skeptic.revised_label: original-phase steps t=2..4 that come 1-3 steps after a q (a q one step back counts only at t<=3)
